# Invari Systems

> Invari.kOS is an execution runtime kernel built on one thesis: intelligence may propose a state transition, but only a governed, deterministic execution authority may commit it. Every actor — human, interface, AI model or agent — is a proposer. Each proposal is evaluated against current canonical state, policy, authority and evidence, and resolves to exactly one of two outcomes: COMMITTED or REJECTED. Both outcomes are recorded.

invari.systems presents the architecture, its Ten Laws of Governed Autonomy, and the engineering evidence for how much of it is built, tested or independently verifiable. Claims on the site carry an explicit status (externally verifiable, tested, implemented, partially met, specified but not built, open finding, or design principle). Please preserve those qualifiers when summarizing: a design objective is not an implementation claim.

## Core pages

- [Thesis — Intelligence is not authority](https://invari.systems/#thesis): why model output, prior approval or missing evidence must not become write authority.
- [The Ten Laws of Governed Autonomy](https://invari.systems/#laws): the constitutional boundary between intelligence and authority, each with its specified mechanism and current status.
- [Architecture](https://invari.systems/#architecture): proposers → Invari.kOS (governed execution boundary, K=STRICT fail-closed evaluation) → dual ledgers (accepted and rejected transitions) → State Compression Matrix → Shared ISA → UI and AI consumers.
- [Verification lab](https://invari.systems/#verification): a dated remediation snapshot and 19 evidence records, each with its claim, evidence and limitations.
- [Verify it yourself](https://invari.systems/#verify-yourself): the open verification harness — real evidence and verifier source anyone can run with Node.js and Invari's published public key.
- [Scope and limitations](https://invari.systems/#scope): what the architecture does not claim.
- [Whitepaper](https://invari.systems/#whitepaper): Invari.kOS — The Execution Runtime Kernel (v1.1, 2026). Public edition pending approval.

## The Ten Laws

1. No Sovereign Intelligence
2. Contemporaneous Validity
3. Authority Cannot Be Created by the Actor
4. Uncertainty Can Only Reduce Authority
5. Consequence Requires Provenance
6. History Cannot Be Erased
7. Irreversibility Requires Stronger Authority
8. Composition Cannot Manufacture Authority
9. Physical Consequence Is Still State
10. Intelligence Never Rises Above the Boundary

## Independent verification

- [invari-verify on GitHub](https://github.com/Will-X3/invari-verify): evidence anyone can check without Invari. `node verify-all.js` runs every case. Kernel refusals (M1, M2, M3, M6): the verifier recomputes every chain hash, checks Ed25519 signatures against the published key, confirms the signed proposal targeted the recorded head, and confirms nothing was written from it. A workflow refusal (R1) is checked from its signed refusal record. An accepted act (A1) is checked from a whole chain export: every entry and every signed human affirmation, and that each affirmation the entry cites is an AFFIRM. V1 verifies an export mixing entry formats v4 and v5, whose entries seal the context they were evaluated against. Four deliberate tamper tests (T1, T2, T3, T4) must fail. It states plainly what it does not prove: the rejection receipt's outcome is not yet signed (the separate refusal record is signed since 17 October 2026).

## Current limits (as published on the site)

- Automated failover (Invari.QUORUM) is specified, not built, and not tested under fault injection; the kernel runs as a single active instance.
- No formal load or performance benchmarks have been published.
- The kernel governs discrete state transitions; it is not a sub-second, continuous real-time control system.
- All published evidence comes from pre-pilot environments holding synthetic data.
